own_solution.law: Each activity obeys A(t)=A(0)2^(-t/T). Equal detection efficiencies cancel when the count rates are equated. Thus t=ln(2400/500)/[ln(2)(1/6-1/72)]=14.8126 h. Adding 170 Bq of the longer-lived isotope to this sample changes its initial activity to 670 Bq, giving t=12.0489 h.
assumptions: The stated half-lives describe exponential radioactive decay with constant decay constants.
The isotopes decay independently without feeding one another, as stated.
The counter has the same nonzero efficiency for both isotopes and detects only decays in this sample, as stated.
Any added activity is specified at the moment of preparation.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T9D9A and TF3A2 omit the added activity's number and unit, whereas the corresponding quantified additions specify 170 Bq, so the variants do not all preserve the required numerical information.

notes: The base problem and each individual extension are physically well-posed. The invalid verdict concerns the required minimal-variant property: 'small batch' and 'small amount' do not specify 170 Bq. The quantified activity variants consistently use 170 Bq, and both efficiency variants consistently use the dimensionless value 0.36. Waste-drum activity is disconnected because the counter explicitly detects only decays in the sample; additions to an earlier sample are likewise disconnected.
